soul.hero_subtitle: History, languages and stories: discover Benin through the people who keep it alive.
soul.hero_note: Content is being reviewed with historians and speakers. Unvalidated items are flagged.

heritage.title: Three places, three memories
heritage.intro: Choose a site and browse its timeline.

abomey.intro: Capital of the Kingdom of Dahomey, Abomey preserves the palaces of its kings, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
abomey.source: UNESCO (Royal Palaces of Abomey); Historical Museum of Abomey. To be completed with academic sources.

events.title: Birth of the kingdom
events.text: The Kingdom of Dahomey took shape around Abomey. King Houégbadja is often associated with this founding period.

events.title: Opening to the coast
events.text: Under King Agadja, Dahomey conquered Allada and then Ouidah, gaining direct access to Atlantic trade.

events.title: The reign of Ghézo
events.text: Ghézo consolidated the state and the army. His reign is one of the most powerful in the kingdom's history.

events.title: The Franco-Dahomean wars
events.text: King Béhanzin resisted the French colonial army. He surrendered in 1894 and was exiled to Martinique.

events.title: UNESCO listing
events.text: The Royal Palaces of Abomey were inscribed on the World Heritage List.

events.title: Return of royal treasures
events.text: France returned 26 works to Benin that had been taken in the 1892 looting.

ouidah.intro: Once a major port of the Atlantic slave trade, Ouidah is now a place of remembrance and the city of Vodun.
ouidah.source: UNESCO (The Slave Route project); history books on the Atlantic slave trade. To be completed.

events.title: The Portuguese fort
events.text: The São João Baptista de Ajudá fort was established in Ouidah. It now houses a history museum.

events.title: Conquest by Dahomey
events.text: Ouidah, in the Hueda kingdom, was conquered by Dahomey under King Agadja.

events.title: Ouidah 92
events.text: First major festival devoted to Vodun cultures and religions.

events.title: The Slave Route
events.text: UNESCO's "The Slave Route" project was launched in Ouidah.

events.title: The Door of No Return
events.text: The monument was inaugurated at the end of the route taken by captives to the beach.

events.title: 10 January
events.text: The national Vodun festival was established in Benin.

portonovo.intro: Official capital of Benin, Porto-Novo is known for its museums and Afro-Brazilian heritage.
portonovo.source: Honmè Museum; Da Silva Museum; Alexandre Sènou Adandé Ethnographic Museum. To be completed.

events.title: Hogbonou
events.text: The city developed under the name Hogbonou, then the Portuguese called it Porto-Novo.

events.title: The French protectorate
events.text: King Sodji signed a protectorate treaty with France.

events.title: Capital of colonial Dahomey
events.text: Porto-Novo became the capital of the Dahomey colony.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Dahomey became independent on 1 August. Porto-Novo remains the official capital, while Cotonou hosts the seat of government.

stories.title: Stories to read and understand
stories.intro: Five entries to better understand what you will see on site.
stories.review: This story touches on living religious practices. It is being reviewed with practitioners and specialists.
respect: Always ask permission before photographing or filming a ceremony or a person.
Follow the instructions of guides and site managers.
Do not touch sacred objects or enter restricted areas.
A contribution or gift is often expected: ask your guide.

cards.title: Béhanzin
cards.summary: The last sovereign king of Dahomey.

chapters.title: The king
chapters.text: Béhanzin reigned from 1889 to 1894, when France was extending its hold on the coast.

chapters.title: Resistance
chapters.text: Between 1892 and 1894, his army fought French colonial troops in the Franco-Dahomean wars.

chapters.title: Exile
chapters.text: Defeated, he was deported to Martinique, then to Algeria, where he died in 1906.

cards.title: The Abomey appliqués
cards.summary: Fabrics that tell the story of the kings.

chapters.title: A court art
chapters.text: Appliqués are cloths decorated with cut-out motifs sewn on, telling key episodes of the reigns.

chapters.title: The emblems
chapters.text: Each king is associated with an animal: the buffalo for Ghézo, the lion for Glèlè, the shark for Béhanzin.

chapters.title: Today
chapters.text: Craftspeople in Abomey keep this art alive and offer pieces to visitors.

chapters.title: A national holiday
chapters.text: Established in 1996, it recognises Vodun as part of the country's cultural and spiritual heritage.

chapters.title: Ouidah on that day
chapters.text: The town hosts ceremonies, dances and processions, bringing together practitioners and visitors.

chapters.title: Attending
chapters.text: Ceremonies are not a show: find out about the rules to respect.

chapters.title: The craft
chapters.text: In Abomey, craftspeople cast brass and bronze using the lost-wax method to make figures.

chapters.title: Gu (Ogou)
chapters.text: In the Vodun tradition, iron and the forge are associated with the deity Gu, also called Ogou.

chapters.title: Meeting the craftspeople
chapters.text: Visiting a workshop helps you understand the steps of the work and directly supports the craftspeople.

chapters.title: What it is
chapters.text: Vodun is a set of beliefs and practices originating in the region. It is practised by many Beninese people.

chapters.title: What it is not
chapters.text: It is not reduced to the "black magic" or "voodoo" of films, which are caricatures.

chapters.title: In practice
chapters.text: To attend a ceremony, go through a local guide and follow the instructions.
